asOfNote: As of 11:40 a.m. on Wednesday, November 25th. The exchange rate reflects the trading base rate announced by the Export-Import Bank of Korea (won/dollar 1,343.60 won, won/yen 843.41 won, won/yuan 201.70 won), and the prices of oil (WTI/Brent January contract), gold, silver, and China's three major futures exchanges are intraday prices. The latest Dubai crude oil and LME official prices are the values ​​as of November 24th (spot settlement prices for zinc, lead, nickel, and tin, and 3-month futures prices for copper and aluminum), and the Public Procurement Service release price is the sales price as of November 25th. China's petrochemical spot (SunSirs), BDI, and CBOT grain prices are as of November 24th, and the CFR Japan (MOPJ) naphtha valuation price as of November 23rd is the latest published value. SCFI and CCFI are released every Friday, so the values ​​as of November 20 are the most recent. Crypto is traded 24 hours a day, so the price is at 11:40 a.m. on November 25th (CoinGecko). For recycled raw materials, the Korea Environment Corporation's monthly survey for October 2026 is the latest, and the November report will be announced on November 26. The latest Bank of Korea price index is from October, and the latest index Nuri petrochemical prices is from the third quarter of 2026.

daily.label: Daily
daily.summary: As of 11:40 am on Wednesday, November 25th. The standard won-dollar trading rate fell slightly to 1,343.60 won (-3.00 won), and oil prices were $80.88 for WTI January contract and $87.67 for January contract for Brent, with Brent falling by 4% in the Asian market. Gold $3,569.05 (-2.4%) and silver $41.29 (-4.6%) also fell from the previous morning, and copper, aluminum, and nickel fell on the LME. Chinese petrochemical spot prices were weak at -5.2% for toluene, -2.8% for benzene, and -2.3% for PP, and the Public Procurement Service's emission prices for copper, aluminum, and tin were all lowered. BDI is 3,068 points (+2.3%), the highest since October 5.

weekly.label: Weekly
weekly.summary: This is the flow as of the morning of the third trading day of the fourth week of November (11/25). Compared to the closing price of the previous Friday (11/20), oil prices have fallen significantly (WTI -3.0%, Brent -5.3%, Dubai -5.5%), and the won is weakened by 1.0% against the dollar (KRW 1,330.80 → KRW 1,343.60). Gold was strengthened to +0.9%, silver was almost flat at +0.1%, and LME was lowered to -1.6% for copper, -2.0% for aluminum, and -1.6% for nickel. BDI rose 5.9% to 3,068 points (highest since October 5), and CBOT grains were mixed at -0.8% for wheat, -0.1% for corn, and +1.1% for soybeans. Chinese petrochemical spot prices are weak at -2.9% for benzene, -1.7% for PP, and -0.5% for PC.

highlights.title: Brent retraces 4% in one day — to $87
highlights.text: Brent January contract rose to $91.40 on 11/24 and then fell to $87.67 in Asian trading on 11/25 (−5.29% on the week). The decline in January WTI contract was small at $80.88 (-3.03% on the week), narrowing the Brent-WTI spread to $6.79.

highlights.title: Gold and silver return part of the previous day’s sharp increase
highlights.text: Spot gold $3,569.05 (−2.4% from the previous morning, +0.87% for the week), silver $41.29 (−4.6%, +0.07% for the week). The price, which had risen to $3,622.55 (London morning notice) in the New York market on 11/24, was reverted.

highlights.title: Won strengthens — trading base rate 1,343.60 won
highlights.text: The won/dollar trading base rate fell by 3.00 won from 1,346.60 won on 11/24 to 1,343.60 won on 11/25 (weekly weakness of +0.96%). The won/yen is 843.41 won, and the won/yuan is 201.70 won.

highlights.title: Public Procurement Service emission price and Chinese spot price fall together
highlights.text: On 11/25, the Public Procurement Service lowered copper to 17,800,000 won (-5.67%), aluminum to 4,590,000 won (-12.4%), and tin to 59,490,000 won (-7.75%). Chinese spot prices are 6,240 yuan (-5.22%) for toluene, 7,320 yuan (-2.75%) for benzene, and 9,916.67 yuan (-2.27%) for PP.

monthly.label: Monthly
monthly.badge: Confirmed in October, tentative in November
monthly.summary: The October confirmed notice and the published values from November 1 to 20 are placed side by side. Oil and copper prices fell significantly in November from their peak in October, and the food index and domestic grain import prices moved slowly.

highlights.title: High in October → Plunge in November
highlights.text: The monthly average for WTI spot is $102.07 in October → $92.71 (−9.2%) from November 1 to 17, and for Brent, it is 123.93 → $95.98 (−22.6%). The futures closing price on November 20 was WTI $83.98, which is lower than the monthly average.

highlights.title: Monthly average for copper -6.4%, aluminum and nickel rise
highlights.text: The LME spot monthly averages fell to 14,532 → $13,608 for copper, 3,820 → $3,792 for zinc, and rose to 3,061 → $3,145 for aluminum and 15,470 → $15,752 for nickel. Copper October averages were the highest of the year.

highlights.title: Food prices fall for the first time in 5 months
highlights.text: The FAO food price index in October was 133.9 (−1.2%), with grains at 116.8 (−4.5%), led by wheat and corn. The domestic import price is $299.69 (-0.13%) for wheat, $273.46 (+1.23%) for corn, and $555.61 (+1.82%) for soybeans.

highlights.title: Exchange rate is flat, NAFTA is -10%
highlights.text: The monthly average of won and dollar is almost unchanged from 1,337.66 won in October to 1,338.91 won from 1 to 20 November. Naphtha (CFR Japan) is -10.4% from 991.98 → $888.69. Petrochemical PC was +1.70% in October and returned to -0.94% in the third week of November.

yearly.label: Yearly
yearly.badge: Compared to the beginning of the year
yearly.summary: Fluctuations through November 20 compared to the end of 2025 (or December 2025 average). Oil prices and shipping rose significantly, and gold hit an all-time high before falling lower than at the beginning of the year.

highlights.title: Oil price +46%, March is a watershed month
highlights.text: WTI is +46.3% from $57.42 at end-2025 to $83.98 on 11/20. Due to the Middle East crisis in March, it soared to $119.48 on March 9 and then went through an adjustment, and is +25.3% compared to the end of February ($67.02).

highlights.title: Gold falls after an all-time high
highlights.text: It hit an all-time high of $5,318.40 (COMEX closing price) on January 29th and fell to $3,515.40 on 11/20, -19.0% compared to the beginning of the year. During the same period, silver fell further by -42.69%.

highlights.title: Copper's increase from +23% increased to +3.6%
highlights.text: Copper rose to a monthly average of $14,532 in October, +23.1% compared to the beginning of the year, but fell sharply in November, reaching a spot price of $12,230.50 (+3.6%) on 11/20. Aluminum +10.7%, zinc +16.1%, nickel +2.9%.

highlights.title: Shipping +54%, exchange rate -7%
highlights.text: BDI is +54.4% from 1,877 to 2,898 at the end of 2025. The won/dollar price was -7.1% from 1,439.0 won to 1,336.2 won, or the monthly average of 1,527.30 won in June was the highest point of the year.

recycled.label: Recycled materials
recycled.summary: This is the October 2026 version of the Nationally Approved Statistics (No. 392001) “Recyclable Resource Price Survey,” which is surveyed by the Korea Environment Corporation on the 10th of every month and published on the 26th. It is the national average, won/kg, including value-added tax and excluding logistics costs. It is the sales price after intermediate processing for waste plastic, waste glass bottles, and waste metal cans, and the purchase price of unprocessed raw materials from intermediate processing companies for waste paper and steel scrap. Among the 26 items, ABS flake was excluded from the table as it was not announced (-) this month.

highlights.title: Aluminum cans -12.6%, waste metals took the largest lead
highlights.text: Aluminum cans fell 361.3 won from 2,863.4 won in September to 2,502.1 won in October. Steel cans fell to 342.7 won (-5.1%), and steel scrap fell to 346.1 won (-3.6%). The LME aluminum average in September was $3,277 per ton, up 0.9% from the previous month, but the price of domestic can compressed products moved in the opposite direction.

highlights.title: PET was divided — colored and composite surged, colorless and compressed remained unchanged.
highlights.text: PET colored flakes rose from KRW 465.8 to KRW 488.6 (+4.9%), and composite flakes rose from KRW 395.8 to KRW 426.5 (+7.8%). On the other hand, colorless flakes showed little change at KRW 1,133.3 (−0.05%) and PET compression stood at KRW 603.2 (−0.3%).

highlights.title: Recycled pellets were weak, only ABS rose.
highlights.text: Subtracting PE pellets of 985.6 won (+0.4%), PP 786.8 won (−0.9%), PS 1,245.0 won (−1.6%), EPS ingots 543.7 won (−1.7%), and EPS pellets all fell 926.1 won (−0.9%). ABS pellets rose from 1,423.3 won to 1,437.0 won (+1.0%).

highlights.title: Paper scrap rose for two consecutive months
highlights.text: Waste corrugated cardboard has been on the rise since August (91.2 won) from 92.9 won to 93.5 won (+0.6 won), and waste newspaper is flat from 125.7 won to 125.8 won. The three colors of waste glass bottles and waste tire rubber powder cost about 0.1 to 3.3 won.

recycled.note: Source/standard: Korea Environment Corporation 「Recyclable Resources Price Survey」, October 2026 (surveyed on 2026-10-10, announced on 2026-10-26), National Approved Statistics No. 392001. It is the average of the prices of survey companies in 8 regions nationwide (excluding Jeju), and the metropolitan area value in each row is the average of Seoul, Incheon, and Gyeonggi. The published price may differ from the actual transaction price depending on the region, quality, processing stage, and transaction conditions, so you must check the research standards for contracts and bids. The next announcement (for November 2026) is scheduled for 2026-11-26. The survey items for this statistics are 2 waste paper, 17 waste plastics (PE·PP·PS·ABS·PVC·PET·EPS), 3 waste glass bottles, 3 waste metals (steel scrap, iron cans, aluminum cans), and 1 waste tire. Engineering resins such as PC, PMMA, and PBT and waste copper (copper) scrap were not investigated and were not loaded.

notes: All prices are confirmed from free and public sources. Paid index-only items are not estimated and not indicated.

LME zinc, lead, nickel, and tin are the LME official spot (Cash) settlement price (11/24: zinc 3,665.00, lead 1,786.00, nickel 15,060.00, tin $40,825.00), and the copper and aluminum in the table are the 3-month futures official price (11/24: copper) 12,055.00·Aluminum $2,789.00), so the standards are different. The source is the Westmetall table, which is a direct translation of the LME official price.
Petrochemical and plastic raw materials are priced at domestic Chinese spot prices (yuan/ton), which differ from Korean import negotiators depending on grade, volume, and freight.

Nafta was carried in two ways. The CFR Japan (MOPJ) public valuation is $809.00/ton (11/23), and the Singapore spot price of Offinet (Korea National Oil Corporation) international petroleum product price is $86.44/barrel (11/23, $727.09 per ton). The units are different so they cannot be compared directly.
BDI, Capesize, Panamax, and Supramax are the Baltic Shipping Exchange indices, and their closing prices are on Tuesday, November 24. We even reflected the announcement made around 21:00 Korean time.

The FAO food and grain price index is a monthly index and is the October 2026 value (announced on November 6). The FAO announcement is 133.9 (−1.6 points, −1.2%) for food and 116.8 (−5.5 points, −4.5%) for grains, which is slightly different from the KREI screen display (−1.7 points for food).

CBOT wheat and corn for December and soybeans for January were loaded with consecutive closing prices in cents/bushel (closing price on 11/24), and the domestic import unit price is dollars/ton based on customs clearance in October 2026 from the Agricultural and Fishery Products Trade Information. International futures prices and domestic customs clearance prices have different freight rates, exchange rates, and payment times, so they should only be compared in the same direction.

Crypto is traded 24 hours a day and has different reference days. The price and fluctuation rate are based on the CoinGecko dollar spot and 24-hour fluctuation rate, and the won price is based on the Upbit won market at the same time.
LME copper and aluminum are based on 3-month futures prices, and spot settlement prices are written in the notes for each item.

The Public Procurement Service's stockpile release price includes VAT and is a sales price within the limits of registered actual consumers, and cannot be directly compared with the LME international price.

Korea Petrochemical Association (KPIA) raw material and resin prices were not included because they cannot be checked for free. kpia.or.kr had a connection error (500·503) and the association's data was moved to kcia.kr (Korea Chemical Industry Association), and the association's price and statistics DB is only for paid users (1.2 million won per year, 2 devices). No estimates were included.

The exchange rate is the trading standard rate announced by the Export-Import Bank of Korea (announced once a business day, around 11 a.m.), and is different from the exchange rate at bank counters and card payments. The 11/25 notice is 1,343.60 won for won/dollar, 843.41 won for won/yen, and 201.70 won for won/yuan, and was cross-checked with the Export-Import Bank Open API Mirror and commercial bank notices (Woori Bank 1,342.90 won, Busan Bank 1,342.35 won). The standard trading rate for each bank differs slightly from the Export-Import Bank notice in decimal units.

Chinese futures are the values ​​of the main contracts of the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE), Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE), and Zhengzhou Commodity Exchange (ZCE) read at the Sina Finance delayed price. This is the intraday value as of the morning of November 25th (11:39 Korean time), and the closing price of the previous day was the closing price of November 24th.
SHFE copper/aluminum is yuan/ton, Shanghai Crude Oil (SC) is yuan/barrel. The LME dollar notation and the exchange rate, VAT, and rating are different, so direct comparison is not possible.
The fluctuations of DCE PP·LLDPE·PVC·EG and ZCE PTA·methanol were calculated as the difference from the closing price on November 24.

SCFI·CCFI is a container freight index released every Friday by the Shanghai Shipping Exchange (SSE). Only the comprehensive index is released, and detailed indices for each route are provided to paid subscribers.

The SMM production copper premium carried the figure specified in the SMM public article (11/23 warrant average of $450/ton, −$45 compared to the previous day). The 11/24 public value could not be confirmed, so the 11/23 value was kept, and the dashboard value is only visible after logging in.

The KOMIS (Korea Resources Information Service) screen could not confirm the values ​​even in this update, so 6 types of non-ferrous metals were filled in with the Westmetall table, which was copied directly from the LME official notice. Spot settlement price and 3-month futures price are shown separately.

Index Nuri petrochemical raw material prices are based on CFR Northeast Asia since 2012 based on a survey by the Korea Chemical Industry Association (KCIA), and the latest value in the public table is the average for the third quarter of 2026 (updated on October 30). This is not the actual price of domestic won.

KAMIS wholesale price is the wholesale market middleman sales price (national average) confirmed as of November 24th (59,640 won for 20 kg of rice product, same after 11/20). For soybeans (40kg of domestically produced white beans), the November 20th survey was the latest confirmed value, so I left it as is.

The Bank of Korea's producer price index and import price index are provisional values for October 2026 (2020=100). The producer price index was announced on November 20th, and the import price index was announced on November 13th.

Import unit prices for the most recent month by item and HS code from the Korea Customs Service's export and import trade statistics (tradedata.go.kr) were not confirmed on the first public screen, so they were not included in this update.

The operation rate and inventory indicators of SCI99 (intl.sci99.com) were not included because they are for paid members only. The PP·LLDPE values ​​from the public price center on the same site are not included in the table because the items overlap with the existing Chinese spot products (SunSirs).

The Korea Nonferrous Metals Association (nonferrous.or.kr) discloses the spot prices of the six LME nonferrous metals (copper, aluminum, zinc, lead, nickel, and tin) and the monthly average and domestic sales prices of zinc ingots. The domestic price of zinc ingots is the standard domestic distribution price excluding VAT provided by Korea Zinc.

The LME inventory, precious metals (gold and silver) prices, and weekly and monthly market status comments on the association site could not be confirmed in the public menu. The statistical information sub-statistics screen of the non-ferrous metal statistics and price information bulletin board could not be opened due to a server error (VBScript 800a0009), so only the price and statistics data posted in the bulletin board was used.

Recycled raw materials are monthly published values from the Korea Environment Corporation’s “Recyclable Resources Price Survey” (National Approved Statistics No. 392001). It is surveyed on the 10th of each month and announced on the 26th, and the unit is KRW/kg (including value-added tax, excluding logistics costs) and is the national average. Waste paper and steel scrap are the purchase price of unprocessed raw materials from intermediate processing companies, and waste plastic, waste glass bottles, and waste metal cans are the sales price after intermediate processing, so the actual transaction price may be different even for the same item.
